structure.title: 2. Building factors using alternative measures of corporate investment
3. Building factors using subcomponents of asset growth
Declaration of competing interest / Data availability / Supplementary material

observations.statement: Frames its estimand as a measurement/construct-validity question: whether HXZ/FF5F factor-model performance is driven by the specific asset-growth construction of the investment factor rather than by investment itself, not a causal treatment-effect design.

Names the maximum-Sharpe-ratio model-comparison framework (Barillas and Shanken 2017; Barillas et al. 2020) as its comparison design, noting that under this framework the choice of test assets does not affect the comparison of two models.
observations.quote: test assets do not matter if our sole purpose is to compare the two models

observations.statement: Discusses the threat that its five chosen alternative investment measures could be cherry-picked, and addresses it by extending the comparison to 144 systematically constructed measure combinations.

Explicitly declines to take a stance on whether findings reflect risk or mispricing, stating this cannot be resolved without a structural model, framing the paper's contribution as comparative/documentary rather than causal.
Ties every reported comparison statistic to a closed-form equation from the cited methodology paper rather than describing the comparison procedure only narratively.
States the sample period repeatedly in table notes rather than in a dedicated data section: spanning regressions and portfolio-return tables specify monthly data from 1972 to 2018.

Has no separate Data or Sample section; data sources, coverage, and construction procedures appear only in footnotes and table notes scattered across sections, with fuller replication of HXZ/FF5F baselines deferred to an online appendix.
States NYSE-based breakpoints (NYSE quintile cutoffs) as the portfolio-formation rule for every sorted-portfolio table, adopted for consistency across tests rather than justified case by case.
Names the external repository location of the underlying data and code in a Data availability statement rather than describing raw data sources or exclusion criteria in the main text body.

Defines asset growth (AG) precisely as the year-on-year percentage change in book value of total assets, and defines each alternative investment measure (CAPX, PPE growth, TOTK, PHK, INTK) with an explicit normalization.
observations.quote: year-on-year percentage change in the book value total assets

observations.statement: Decomposes AG into eleven mutually exclusive balance-sheet subcomponents (six asset-side, five liability/equity-side), each defined by an accounting identity in a footnote and normalized by lagged total assets so components sum exactly to AG.

Constructs total, physical, and intangible capital measures following a cited method that adds off-balance-sheet capitalized R&D and a fixed share of SG&A as intangible investment, explicitly flagging that assumption as one used in prior studies.

Transforms macroeconomic shock variables heterogeneously by source: several series use AR(1) residuals to isolate an unexpected component, others are used directly as return spreads or pre-built innovations, with the choice stated for every variable.

Defines equity and debt issuance (mechanism outcomes) from standard balance-sheet items, scales them by lagged total assets, and winsorizes at the 1st and 99th percentiles, the only explicit winsorization mentioned in the main text.

Constructs an aggregate overextrapolation index from survey-based return expectations via a recursively estimated nonlinear-least-squares decay parameter, with the estimation procedure and data source described in a single long footnote.

Structures maximum-Sharpe-ratio comparison tables as baseline-model-by-alternative-model matrices with point estimates and asymptotic p-values in parentheses, omitting N and R2 since the test is not a regression.
Reports observation counts and R2 for every column of the spanning regressions alongside coefficients and t-statistics, with no fixed effects listed and no separate mean-of-dependent-variable row.
States the standard-error type directly in the note beneath every spanning-regression table rather than only describing it in the main text.
Reports sum-of-squared and mean-absolute pricing errors (annualized) in the GMM pricing tables in place of R2, alongside t-statistics rather than raw standard errors.
States value-weighted portfolio returns and NYSE breakpoints directly in the table title or note for every sorted-portfolio result, making the weighting scheme explicit.

States that spanning-regression standard errors follow the Newey and West (1987) heteroskedasticity-and-autocorrelation correction with up to 12 lags, without separately justifying the choice of 12 lags beyond citing the procedure.

Computes significance for the maximum-Sharpe-ratio tests from asymptotic p-value formulas in a companion methodology paper, cited by equation number, with no discussion of finite-sample behavior or a bootstrap alternative.
States that the GMM pricing tests use an identity weighting matrix at a first-stage estimation, a specific choice stated in the main text but not compared against an alternative weighting scheme.

Reports sum-of-squared and mean-absolute pricing errors as the fit diagnostic for every stochastic-discount-factor specification, annualized for comparability across factors measured at different frequencies.

Splits the main Sharpe-ratio comparisons by above- versus below-median values of an overextrapolation index as a diagnostic showing the AG-model advantage is confined to one subsample rather than holding uniformly.
Discloses in a footnote an unreported check of the performance gap between the five best-fitting alternative models and the AG-based model, without showing the underlying numbers.

Addresses robustness to normalizing-variable choice for the two traditional investment measures through six named alternative normalizations, reported as qualitatively unchanged in an unreported test disclosed only in a footnote.

Presents a 144-measure model-mining exercise as a dedicated robustness subsection with its own histogram figure, framed explicitly as verifying the main finding is not driven by the choice of five specific alternative measures.

Checks the spanning-regression conclusion against being spanned by each AG subcomponent individually and by an aggregated remainder factor, with the fully disaggregated version pointed to an appendix table not present in the extracted text.

Checks the debt-equity substitution finding in an unreported test using single-sorted rather than bivariate-sorted portfolios, disclosed as qualitatively similar in a footnote rather than shown in a table.

Organizes the macro-factor pricing results around a between-portfolio-group contrast, comparing which of twelve candidate macro shocks price AG/INVT/AREC portfolios versus PPE portfolios, treated as the central differentiating result rather than a firm-level subgroup split.

Uses debt-versus-equity issuance behavior in high- versus low-sentiment periods as an intermediate-outcome test of a proposed debt-equity substitution mechanism connecting AG, INVT, and AREC to equity-financing-cost exposure.
Explicitly labels its overextrapolation-based evidence for a behavioral origin of financing costs as suggestive rather than causal.
observations.quote: suggestive (though by no means causal) evidence

observations.statement: Partially rules out technology/productivity-shock explanations for the AG/INVT/AREC advantage by showing those shocks also price PPE portfolios, so they fail to differentiate the groups the paper is explaining.

Interprets the relative size of the debt-equity substitution effect through cross-group percent-change comparisons of equity- versus debt-issuance responses across AG/INVT/AREC quintiles against PPE quintiles, rather than through standard-deviation units or a dollar-cost translation.
States it is difficult to definitively conclude whether a factor model captures risk or mispricing absent a structural model, repeating this caveat in both the introduction and the conclusion.
observations.quote: difficult to definitively conclude that a given factor model captures risk or mispricing

observations.statement: Flags its review of the macroeconomic-shock literature underlying the chosen factor list as necessarily incomplete, limiting any claim that the tested shocks are exhaustive.

Explicitly declines to take a position on which specific driver of equity-financing costs (agency frictions, risk aversion, or behavioral biases) explains its results, treating that question as outside the paper's scope.

Presents both main-text figures as histograms of a single test statistic (maximum squared Sharpe ratio) across many alternative models, with colored vertical reference lines marking specific benchmark models, a convention distinct from event-study or RD-style plots.

Uses the same stars convention in every table note, spelling out the same three conventional significance thresholds, uniformly across Sharpe-ratio, regression, and GMM tables despite their different statistical frameworks.
Writes table notes to be self-contained, restating exact variable-construction formulas such as debt and equity issuance definitions rather than only cross-referencing the main text.
Previews every major finding in the introduction in the order the later sections present them, with footnotes pointing ahead to specific tables.

Has no separate Robustness section; alternative-measure and alternative-specification checks are embedded as subsections within the same numbered sections as the corresponding main result, with further checks deferred to a cited online appendix.

Organizes the paper as a chain of sections that each resolve one sub-question in sequence (which alternative measures matter, then which AG subcomponents matter, then which macro shocks matter, then what mechanism explains it), with the conclusion restating the chain.
Opens the introduction with a contribution paragraph framing the paper as challenging the theoretical interpretation of the HXZ/FF5F investment factors, rather than presenting a new return anomaly.
States, in a Data availability statement, a Mendeley Data DOI as the location where the paper's code and data can be found, an explicit citable replication-package pointer.

Draws on standard commercial/licensed financial databases (implied by Compustat-style variable names) combined with numerous third-party macro-factor series each cited to its own source paper, rather than restricted or hand-collected firm-level data; no data-use agreement is mentioned.
Points to supplementary material via the article's own DOI as a location separate from the Mendeley code/data DOI, though its contents (Tables E1-E14) are not reproduced in the extracted main text.

concordance.paper_says: Maximum Sharpe ratio comparison tests (Barillas and Shanken 2017; Barillas et al. 2020) are the primary model-comparison method in Sections 2-3 and Tables 9-10.
concordance.card_shows: Design d4 records method other:maximum_sharpe_ratio_test with bias-adjusted Sharpe ratio and asymptotic p-values, traced to Barillas_Shanken_maxSR_Test.ado.

concordance.paper_says: The 17 pages of main text read never name Fama-MacBeth or a two-step cross-sectional regression as an empirical method.
concordance.card_shows: Design d2 and specifications s1-s2 record a Fama-MacBeth two-step cross-sectional estimator (xtfmb_mion.ado) as one of the paper's methods.
concordance.note: Fama-MacBeth may appear in the online Appendix Section A (Tables E1-E2), which is referenced by footnote but not included in the extracted text.

concordance.paper_says: Spanning regressions (Tables 3-5) state standard errors are corrected for heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation using the Newey and West (1987) procedure with up to 12 lags.
concordance.card_shows: Specification s2 (xtfmb_mion second step) records se.type=hac_newey_west with lag as an unresolved parameter.

concordance.paper_says: No cross-sectional/iid standard-error procedure for a Fama-MacBeth first step is described anywhere in the main text read.
concordance.card_shows: Specification s1 records se.type=iid as the default xtfmb_mion behavior (mvreg step) when no lag is specified.

concordance.paper_says: Table notes state regressions and portfolio tests use monthly data from 1972 to 2018.
concordance.card_shows: pipeline.sample_restrictions records only a generic non-missing-return filter (ret!=.) with no explicit sample-period value.

concordance.paper_says: Portfolio breakpoints throughout use NYSE cutoffs, e.g. NYSE quintile sorts on profitability and each investment measure.
concordance.card_shows: Design d1 implementation_features lists NYSE-based breakpoints for portfolio formation.

concordance.paper_says: Spanning regressions control for the remaining factors in the HXZ model (ME, INV, ROE) or the FF5F model (ME, BM, PROF, INV) alongside the market factor.
concordance.card_shows: Design d3 implementation_features records the AG factor added to HXZ (ME, INV, ROE) and FF5F (ME, BM, FFOP, INV) factor lists.

concordance.paper_says: Table titles and notes specify value-weighted (VW) portfolio returns are used in the GMM pricing tests.
concordance.card_shows: None of the extracted specifications (s1, s2, s3, s5) record a weights value; all are null.

concordance.paper_says: GMM pricing tables report sum of squared pricing errors (SSQE) and mean absolute pricing errors (MAPE), annualized for comparability, as the fit diagnostic for every SDF specification.
concordance.card_shows: The card's diagnostics array is empty; no fit-statistic record was extracted from the traced code files.

concordance.paper_says: A dedicated 144-measure model-mining robustness exercise (Section 2.2) is presented with its own figure to show the main comparison is not sensitive to the choice of alternative investment measures.
concordance.card_shows: The card's robustness array is empty; this exercise was not captured by the files read for the card.

concordance.paper_says: The main text contains ten numbered tables (Tables 1-10) and two figures (Figs. 1-2).
concordance.card_shows: The card's outputs.tables and outputs.figures arrays are both empty.

concordance.paper_says: The Data availability statement names a Mendeley Data DOI (10.17632/tzxtm6ys99.1) as the location of the paper's code and data.
concordance.card_shows: The card's data array is empty, but the traced code path (code/mendeley_tzxtm6ys99_v1/...) embeds the same Mendeley identifier tzxtm6ys99, consistent with the paper's stated location.

gaps: No dedicated summary-statistics table (means/SDs of key variables) found anywhere in the 17 pages of main text read.

No explicit description in the main text of sample-construction filters typical of asset-pricing studies (e.g., minimum price, exchange listing, exclusion of financial firms); such detail may be confined to the online appendix (Tables E1-E14), referenced repeatedly but not included in the extracted text.
No justification given for the specific choice of a 12-lag Newey-West correction.
No discussion of cross-sectional dependence or standard-error clustering beyond the time-series Newey-West adjustment; not flagged as a limitation by the authors.
No preregistration, IRB approval, or research-ethics statement; not applicable to this archival financial-data study and not commented on by the authors.
No explicit external-validity or generalization discussion (e.g., to non-U.S. markets, periods outside 1972-2018, or test assets beyond U.S. equities).
No back-of-envelope dollar-value, cost-benefit, or elasticity translation of the Sharpe-ratio or GMM pricing-error magnitudes.

Online appendix content (Section A, Section D, Tables E1-E14) referenced by footnote roughly a dozen times could not be read; the 17-page extracted text contains only the main body and reference list, with no in-document appendix.

reading.note: Read the entire 17-page extracted text (title/abstract through references) in full, including all footnotes and table notes. The document itself contains no in-text appendix: the 'Appendix. Supplementary material' section on page 16 is only a DOI pointer to online supplementary material (Section A, Section D, Tables E1-E14) that is hosted separately and was not provided for this reading task.
